sections.title: Explanation
sections.content: Szeretnék is built from szeret (to like/love) plus the conditional ending -nék, not the ordinary present-tense -k. That's what makes it sound like 'I would like' instead of a flat 'I like'.
Don't confuse szeretek (I like, present tense) with szeretnék (I would like, conditional) — the extra -né- is what softens the request.
